<!-- Shared BODY for the IPBES_Label_Funnel_Report report family.
     Rendered only via the generated wrapper .qmd files that `{{< include >}}`
     this file -- see R/generate_report_wrappers.R and config.yaml's `reports:`
     section. The leading underscore keeps Quarto from rendering it on its own
     -- but it also keeps it out of the project entirely, so tar_quarto() never
     scans this file for dependencies. That is why the tar_read() calls live in
     the wrapper and arrive here as `report_deps`; `params$...` likewise comes
     from the wrapper. -->

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# Self-contained-report helper, same idiom as IPBES_Fact_Checker.qmd's setup
# chunk -- but report_files_dir is built from params$label/params$assessment_id/
# params$granularity, NOT knitr::current_input(). This qmd is rendered once
# per (assessment, label, granularity) combination via
# quarto::quarto_render(output_file=, execute_params=); current_input()
# always returns the SOURCE filename ("IPBES_Label_Funnel_Report"), which
# would collide every render onto the same _files/ directory.
#
# Inlined rather than sourced from R/branch_helpers.R's granularity_suffix()/
# nli_model_suffix(): quarto::quarto_render() runs this file in its own
# fresh R session, which doesn't inherit _targets.R's lapply(source) of
# R/*.R -- this qmd has never sourced project R/ helpers (only library()
# calls), so a one-line inline copy is more consistent than introducing
# that pattern here.
gran_suffix <- paste0("_", params$granularity)
model_suffix <- if (identical(params$nli_active, "deberta_zeroshot")) "" else paste0("_", params$nli_active)
# file.path("output/reports", ...) rather than a bare name: the qmd source
# lives in input/reports/, but the rendered .html gets moved to
# output/reports/ by the _targets.R target after this chunk runs (Quarto
# renders next to the input regardless of execute_dir) -- writing the
# sidecar directly into its final home means it's already correctly a
# sibling of the .html once that move happens.
report_files_dir <- file.path("output/reports", paste0("IPBES_", params$label, "_Report_", params$assessment_id, model_suffix, gran_suffix, "_files"))
# Wipe before repopulating: copy_into_report_files() only copies in what it's
# given, so a file dropped from one run's inputs (e.g. a removed funnel
# level) would otherwise linger here forever across re-renders.
unlink(report_files_dir, recursive = TRUE, force = TRUE)
dir.create(report_files_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
copy_into_report_files <- function(paths) {
  file.copy(paths, report_files_dir, overwrite = TRUE)
  file.path(basename(report_files_dir), basename(paths))
}

# Target names are label-specific (refutes_funnel_data / supports_funnel_data,
# etc.) rather than one generic target. This used to use tar_read_raw() with a
# name computed from params$label -- but tarchetypes cannot see through that
# (it warns about exactly this), so the funnel report contributed NO dependency
# edges and the old render target had to list them by hand. Both label variants
# are named LITERALLY in the generated WRAPPER instead (Quarto excludes this
# underscore-prefixed body from the project, so it is never scanned for
# dependencies), and each wrapper names only its own label's three targets.
# Matched by exact basename (not a loose grepl) against the deterministic
# filename the R builders produce -- necessary now that "naive_bm" (no
# suffix) and "complete_bm" ("_complete_bm" suffix) coexist on disk and a
# suffix-less grepl for e.g. "_GA1.rds" would also match "_GA1_complete_bm.rds"
# style names as a false substring hit in the wrong direction, or vice versa.
# The wrapper already resolved this label's own targets (refutes_* or
# supports_*) into report_deps, so there is nothing to branch on here.
funnel_target <- function(kind) report_deps[[kind]]

target_stem <- tolower(params$label)
expected_name <- function(kind, ext) sprintf("%s_funnel_%s_%s%s%s.%s", target_stem, kind, params$assessment_id, model_suffix, gran_suffix, ext)

data_path <- funnel_target("data") |>
  (\(x) x[basename(x) == expected_name("data", "rds")])()
# config.yaml's `reports:` declares every (assessment x granularity)
# combination, but a granularity that has not been scored yet produces no rds
# at all -- which is different from an rds that exists and reports x$empty,
# and used to abort the whole project render on the first such combination
# rather than just that document. Both degrade to the same empty-state
# section below (see the `empty-check` chunk). This is expected, not a bug:
# see TODO.md on complete_bm/atomic_bm branches being empty until those
# granularities are actually run.
data_path <- data_path[file.exists(data_path)]
x <- if (length(data_path) == 1L) readRDS(data_path) else list(empty = TRUE)

fig_paths <- copy_into_report_files(
  funnel_target("figures") |>
    (\(x) x[grepl(paste0("_", params$assessment_id, model_suffix, gran_suffix, "\\.png$"), x)])()
)
fig_overall <- fig_paths[grepl("_overall_", fig_paths)]
fig_by_bm <- fig_paths[grepl("_by_bm_", fig_paths) & !grepl("_normalized_", fig_paths)]
fig_by_bm_norm <- fig_paths[grepl("_by_bm_normalized_", fig_paths)]

table_paths <- copy_into_report_files(
  funnel_target("tables") |>
    (\(x) x[grepl(paste0("_", params$assessment_id, model_suffix, gran_suffix, "\\.html$"), x)])()
)
table_l3 <- table_paths[grepl("_l3_", table_paths)]
```

# `r params$label` Funnel — `r params$assessment_id`

## Methodology

Every work discovered by the snowball search under a Background Message
(BM) is put through a 3-level sieve, each level a **subset** of the one
before it, counted as **distinct citing works per (assessment, km, bm)** —
a work cited under two different BMs is two separate findings, not one, so
per-BM counts sum to the assessment-wide total shown below.

1. **Snowball corpus** — every citing work discovered for that BM (the
   forward/citing direction of the snowball search).
2. **NLI `r params$label` (certain)** — of those, works with at least one
   claim scored `` label == "`r params$label`" `` with `uncertain == FALSE`
   by the zero-shot NLI model (Phase 1 — see
   [TD_BM_NLI_approach](TD_BM_NLI_approach.html)).
3. **LLM-confirmed `r params$label`** — of those, works where OpenRouter's
   LLM review (Phase 2 — see
   [TD_NLI_LLM_two_phase](TD_NLI_LLM_two_phase.html)) independently agreed
   with the `r params$label` verdict (`llm_agrees == TRUE`).

There is deliberately no further "+ sufficient evidence" level: Phase 2's
own verification logic forces its `llm_label` to `NOT_ENOUGH_INFO` whenever
it judges the evidence insufficient, so an LLM verdict of `r params$label`
already *implies* sufficient evidence — a separate level here would always
contain exactly the same works as level 3.

**NLI model: `r params$nli_active`.** Level 2/3 counts below reflect
whichever model was active in `input/config.yaml`'s `nli.active` when this
report was rendered — different models are not directly comparable
work-for-work either, since each has its own score distribution and
`uncertain_threshold` calibration (see `TD_BM_NLI_approach.qmd`).

**Claim granularity: `r params$granularity`.** `naive_bm` (the default)
segments each BM's `bm_description`/`bm_label` into evidence-delimited
sub-claims (2-17 per BM) at the sentence level. `complete_bm` instead
treats each field as a single, whole claim (2 per BM, or 1 if
`bm_label`/`bm_description` are identical) — cheaper to score (~71% fewer
NLI pairs measured across both assessments), at the cost of losing which
specific part of a longer BM a citing work actually supports or
contradicts, and of the resulting hypothesis text sometimes exceeding the
NLI model's own token limit (see `TD_BM_NLI_approach.qmd` for the measured
numbers and caveats). Level 2/3 counts below reflect whichever granularity
this report was rendered for; the two are **not** directly comparable
work-for-work, since they're scored against different claim text.

**Phase 2 (LLM verification) is a partial, ongoing process** — OpenRouter
credit has run out mid-run at least once already, so level 3 below
reflects only the pairs reviewed so far, not the full `r params$label`-certain
set from level 2. This number will grow as `llm_verification_parquet` gets
more OpenRouter runs; re-render this report after a rerun rather than
treating today's snapshot as final.

```{r}
#| label: empty-check
#| results: asis
if (isTRUE(x$empty)) {
  cat("No data available yet for this assessment — the snowball, NLI, or LLM verification stage hasn't produced output here.\n\n")
  knitr::knit_exit()
}
```

## Level 3: LLM-confirmed `r params$label`

Every citing work where the LLM's own independent review agreed with NLI's
`r params$label` verdict (and, by construction, judged the evidence for it
sufficient — see Methodology). Use the BM dropdown in the filter row below
the header to narrow to one Background Message.

```{r}
#| label: level3-table
#| results: asis
if (length(table_l3)) {
  cat(sprintf(
    '<iframe src="%s" width="100%%" height="800px" style="border:none;"></iframe>\n\n',
    table_l3
  ))
}
```
